sources.note: Nothing; the 'Afawa' entry (p. 3) is purely ethnographic ('They speak the same language, which is rapidly being replaced by Haussa'). Glottolog's grammar sketch tag is not borne out for Pa'a.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Paʼa language' (accessed 2026-09-17), phonology section sourced to Skinner 1979.
sources.note: Gives consonants, five vowels short/long, diphthongs ei/au, and 'Pa'a also has four tones; high, mid, low, and falling.' No statement about stress.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken et al. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the West Chadic North Bauchi Languages of Bauchi and Jigawa States, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-010. SIL International. 123 pp.
sources.note: Most recent primary fieldwork on Pa'a (two dialect wordlists, Zakara and Tiffi); transcription conventions section may note tone/stress marking. Open access on sil.org but could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Skinner, A. Neil. 1977. North Bauchi Chadic languages: common roots. Afroasiatic Linguistics 4(1): 1-49. Malibu: Undena Publications.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'The phonetic inventory' (p. 5) covers all North Bauchi languages incl. Pa'a: 'As for tones, usually three levels and a falling were heard in the recordings and a number of minimal pairs of monosyllables confirmed, but it would have been highly impressionistic to have included any tonal markings in the present work.' No mention of stress or accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent full text).
